notes: Primary owner of this crossover is superparamagnetism. The comparison with a thin-film mirror in the first version is withdrawn.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³. KV = 25 kT at 300 K gives V = 2.1–2.4e-26 m³: a sphere 3.4–3.6 nm across or a cube 2.8–2.9 nm on a side. The single-domain diameter is about 200–300 nm.
implied_text: The smallest grain that holds its direction at room temperature on laboratory time is a few nanometres across. Real magnets sit two orders of magnitude above that, so thermal erasure of whole grains is not what limits them. Soft matrices lack the barrier.
description: The thermal-stability size of the latch cell is a few nanometres for Nd2Fe14B. It depends on the waiting time chosen and is not a cliff.
value_text: V ≈ 2.1–2.4e-26 m³ (3.4–3.6 nm sphere); KV = 25 kT
notes: The first version called this volume ~30 nm; a 30 nm cube is about 29 000 kT. 25 kT is the convention for a 100 s measurement. value_si is mid-range.

observed_text: A usable motor force is F = ∇(m·B) from a large aligned population. There is no universal millimetre-scale cliff.
implied_text: Macroscopic force is synchronized output of many latched grains. Force scales with aligned moment; the sharp cliff stays at the grain.
description: The sample envelope is a capacity, not a second spatial cliff. No single minimum N for a usable force is extracted.
value_text: force scales with aligned m; no universal N

observed_text: Maximum phonon frequencies sit in the few-to-tens-of-THz class (Al’s spectrum ends near 10 THz; diamond’s near 40 THz). Si zone-centre Raman is 15.5 THz; diamond 40 THz (1332 cm⁻¹). Acoustic clocks run from zero up to the zone-boundary frequency of that branch.
implied_text: ω_s(q) is the allowed-clock table. Nothing in the lattice oscillates as a phonon faster than the highest measured branch.
description: The lattice’s mechanical clocks are the measured branches, from acoustic zero up to a material-typical THz ceiling.
value_text: few–tens of THz (Al ~10 THz; diamond ~40 THz)
notes: value_si is Al’s ~10 THz ceiling as a representative. Optical zone-centre pins: Si 15.5 THz; diamond 40 THz.

observed_text: QSA takes the measured ω(q) as data. Force-constant models that fit the curves are not promoted to node rules. The mapping does not predict which crystal will soften.
implied_text: Branch frequencies are located as the clock table but not derived from a more primitive set of node spring constants.
description: The allowed-clock map is taken, not computed from node springs. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium: hardware scale is not a single number; binary macros belong to related lattice entries.

observed_text: Inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering return discrete ω(q) peaks along each branch. Acoustic long-wave slopes match measured sound speeds (Al longitudinal ≈ 6.4 km s⁻¹; Si [100] longitudinal ≈ 8.4 km s⁻¹). Zone-centre optical pins include Si 15.5 THz and diamond 40 THz.
implied_text: The stable output is the measured surface ω_s(q), its long-wave speeds v_s, and its zone-centre optical frequencies, for as long as the crystal remains ordered.
description: The synchronized ion grid emits a material-typical allowed-clock map, not a single binary macro.
value_text: ω_s(q); v_s; Γ optical pins (Si 15.5 THz; diamond 40 THz)
notes: Long-wave slope is also speed-of-sound. Do not invent a single dispersion cliff.

observed_text: The harmonic restoring energy of a mode is ½ħω(2n+1) (or ½ku² classically). Softening to ω→0 is loss of that restoring constraint along one coordinate.
implied_text: This is an oscillator budget, not an activation barrier that holds a directional state. Dispersion is not a latch.
description: Phonon branches are driven oscillators, not a memory. There is no static barrier holding a written mechanical state.
notes: Negative latch spec: contrast with permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: Driving above the highest lattice frequency produces no additional phonon mode. Zone-boundary / reststrahlen / neutron cutoff sits at the few-to-tens-of-THz class. q outside the first zone is an alias, not a new clock.
implied_text: Drive faster than the last branch → no additional lattice mode.
description: The allowed-clock table ends at the zone-boundary maximum; faster drive is not a phonon.
value_text: ω above last branch (Al ~10 THz; diamond ~40 THz)
notes: Physical ceiling is owned here; Debye ω_D is the continuum stand-in filed under debye-cutoff.

observed_text: Loss of Bragg order ends the map. Melting or amorphization removes the discrete ω(q) branches. Finite lifetime / mean free path blurs a peak but does not erase the branch until the lattice itself fails.
implied_text: The clock table is carried by the crystal. Destroy the grid and the map ends.
description: Melting or amorphization erases the allowed-clock table by destroying the lattice that defined q.
notes: Primary owner of the thermal coexistence cliff is melting.

observed_text: A restoring branch can fall toward ω=0 as a structural transition is approached. An imaginary harmonic ω is the statement that the current lattice is mechanically unstable.
implied_text: Softening to ω→0 closes that restoring channel; a structural transition follows. This is not the first-order melting of Al or W.
description: A branch that loses its restoring frequency is a coordinate-specific grid instability, not the melting cliff.
notes: Soft-mode trajectories are high as a class and medium for any one crystal’s T-axis. Melting owns Bragg-order loss.

observed_text: One primitive cell already defines an optical zone-centre clock; a well-defined q is a phase relation across many cells. Amorphous solids retain a vibrational density of states but lose sharp ω(q) branches. There is no single nanometre cliff.
implied_text: The hardware is the crystalline lattice. The map as a spectrum is an extended-crystal object, not a 10–20 nm buffer.
description: Phonon dispersion requires an ordered grid; one cell sets an optical clock, but the spectrum is many-cell. Amorphization is loss of the map, not a thickness failure.
value_text: primitive cell + extended crystal; no nm cliff
notes: Contrast reflection’s connected-film buffer. Lattice constants in file: Si 5.43 Å; Al 4.05 Å; diamond 3.57 Å.

observed_text: Generation follows the optical cycle (femtoseconds).
implied_text: Generation, when allowed, is already complete on any laboratory shutter. Bias does not replace this clock; it only reads the carriers.
description: Pair generation latency sits in the femtosecond optical-cycle neighbourhood.
notes: Same generation clock class as semiconductor-gap-absorption.

observed_text: τ spans nanoseconds in many direct-gap or dirty samples to milliseconds in high-purity Si. No single universal τ is claimed. Chopping faster than 1/τ rolls off the photocurrent. Gain Γ = τ/t_tr multiplies the current; it does not move Eg.
implied_text: The readout clock is the recombination lifetime τ and the transit time t_tr. Gain is this pair of clocks written as a performance number.
description: τ is a performance metric, not a threshold. Clock overrun of the readout is not closure of Eg.
notes: value_si is a mid-class marker of the stated ns–ms window. Lifetime is high as a class and sample-specific as a number.

observed_text: QSA does not here derive τ from a primitive node count. Lifetime is taken as a measured recombination resource. Gain figures of a given detector are therefore performance data, not predicted constants.
implied_text: The threshold mapping does not depend on closing that derivation.
description: Eg is located; τ and gain are taken as measured performance, not derived.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step.

observed_text: A light-dependent conductance whose spectral onset tracks Eg or Et, with magnitude set by η, α, τ, and μ, reverting when generation stops. Δn = Gτ.
implied_text: Stable output is a reversible, light-dependent conductance, not a latched state and not an ejected vacuum current.
description: The machine’s product is Δσ(hν) that turns on at the gap and reverts when generation stops.
value_text: Δσ onset at Eg or Et; reverts when light off
notes: Photoelectric-threshold and work-function-thermionic eject the carrier into vacuum; this entry keeps it inside the solid.

observed_text: Intrinsic photoconductivity is gated by the same gaps as semiconductor-gap-absorption: Si Eg ≈ 1.12 eV, Ge ≈ 0.66 eV, GaAs ≈ 1.42 eV, diamond ~5.5 eV (all 300 K). Extrinsic photoconductivity is gated by a trap depth Et < Eg.
implied_text: The operating gate is Eg (intrinsic) or Et (extrinsic). Bias does not replace the gate; it only reads the carriers. Thermal generation across the same gate produces dark current.
description: Photoconductivity is the same Eg gate as gap absorption, read as current rather than as opacity.
value_text: Si Eg ≈ 1.12 eV (300 K); or Et < Eg extrinsic
notes: Must share this collapse energy with semiconductor-gap-absorption. value_si is Si at 300 K.

observed_text: τ too short → generated carriers vanish before they contribute a measurable Δσ. Absorption without photocurrent is allowed.
implied_text: The gate opened; the output did not last. That is a readout-clock failure, not a denial of Eg.
description: Clock starvation of the readout leaves the spectral gate intact.
value_text: τ too short vs t_tr / measurement
notes: Blocking contacts or a vanished bias likewise remove the current readout without closing Eg.

observed_text: Below Eg (or Et) this conversion does not occur. Below the edge, extra light of that colour does not raise the current through this channel. Conductance stays at the dark baseline.
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below Eg the photoconductive gate stays shut.
notes: Sub-gap current, if any, is thermal, two-photon, or defect-assisted — other channels. Raising T buries Δσ in dark current: a thermal failure of readout, not a shift of the optical gate to zero.

observed_text: The conversion event is one absorbed photon promoting one electron (and a hole) across Eg or Et. There is no collective optical-buffer analogue of the 10–20 nm mirror. Thinning the absorber reduces the generation volume in proportion to 1−e^{−αL}.
implied_text: A measurable current is the summed drift of a large generated population between contacts. The crystal must be intact enough to support bands or defined traps, and contacted.
description: The gate is a single-event conversion inside an intact, contacted crystal. Thickness is a generation capacity, not a continuity cliff.
notes: Absorption without photocurrent (very short τ, bad contacts) and photocurrent without strong opacity (thin extrinsic layers) are both allowed.

observed_text: Streaking delays of tens to hundreds of attoseconds. Intensity sets rate, not one-event latency.
implied_text: The conversion is finished on any optical-cycle-averaged laboratory clock.
description: Single-electron conversion latency sits in the attosecond regime.

observed_text: Face dependence and contamination shift φ by tenths of an eV. QSA takes measured φ as the gate.
implied_text: No derivation of the 2–6 eV class from a surface-dipole plus chemical-potential construction.
description: The gate is located and shown to be a surface resource; its value is not derived from node rules.
notes: Do not identify φ with Ag’s 3.9 eV optical plasma edge.

observed_text: A material- and face-typical φ, zero photocurrent below it, linear Kmax(ν) above it.
implied_text: The stable output is the threshold itself plus the above-threshold kinetic-energy line.
description: The machine’s stable product is a work-function gate and a linear surplus-energy line.

observed_text: Typical φ 2–6 eV (Cs low, Pt high). KE = hν − φ above threshold.
implied_text: φ is the load-bearing gate. Below it (linear regime) conversion does not occur. Not a latch; the electron leaves.
description: The photoelectric effect is a single-particle energy gate at the work function.
notes: value_si is ~4 eV in joules, mid-class.

observed_text: hν < φ → no linear photoemission (only a Fowler tail exponential in (φ−hν)/kT).
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below the work function the gate stays shut.

observed_text: A single conversion event is already the microscopic effect. Photoemission persists from atomically thin or adsorbate-covered emitters once hν clears φ.
implied_text: No collective buffer is required. One electron at a surface is the hardware. Escape depth limits collection, not the on/off of the gate.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the gate is single-particle. Contrast with reflection’s 10–20 nm stack.
notes: How to query effects that do not need a spatial buffer.

observed_text: The mechanical side follows the acoustic clocks of elasticity and speed-of-sound; the electrical side follows the dielectric response. No clock number is filed in this entry.
implied_text: Device latency is the acoustic transit / plate resonance, not an atomic piezo clock.
description: No single atomic piezo period is extracted. Laboratory clocks sit at the plate resonance.
notes: Cross-cite speed-of-sound and refraction-dielectric. No source opened for a device resonance.

observed_text: The mapping takes measured d_ijk. The factor of 270 between quartz d11 and PZT5H d33 is not derived, and in ceramics part of the coefficient is domain-wall motion.
implied_text: The symmetry gate and T_C collapse are located; the magnitude of d is taken, not computed.
description: Coupling magnitude is a handbook input. That is the principal reason the mapping is medium rather than high.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Polar latch is a different machine sharing the same crystal.

observed_text: Quartz d11 = 2.25–2.31 pm/V. AlN d33 = 5.6 pm/V (single crystal), 3.4–5.15 (polycrystalline). BaTiO3 d33 = 85.6 (crystal), 190 pC/N (ceramic). PZT d33 = 225–618 pC/N across PZT8, PZT4, PZT5A, PZT5H. PVDF d33 = −21 to −27 pC/N.
implied_text: A linear, reversible strain ↔ polarization conversion with a material-typical d_ij, present only while the inversion-free (and, if ferroelectric, polar) lattice holds.
description: The coupling output is a pC/N-class d_ij: quartz ~2, PZT ~10², only inside the symmetry / polar envelope.
value_text: quartz 2.3; AlN 3.4–5.6; BaTiO3 86–190; PZT 225–618; PVDF −21 to −27 pC/N
notes: value_si is quartz d11. BaTiO3 crystal, LiNbO3 and PVDF values are from a tertiary list; the BaTiO3 ceramic value is a search excerpt.

observed_text: The existence condition is the crystal class, not an energy barrier. Quartz needs no poling. A ferroelectric ceramic is poled slightly below its Curie point and loses the poled state above it.
implied_text: Linear piezo is a symmetry-gated coupling, not a memory. Ferroelectric remnant P is a different machine sharing some crystals.
description: No piezo latch. The gate is inversion-free symmetry; quartz does not die with a remnant-P write.
value_text: inversion-free gate; not a KV / P_r latch
notes: Cross-cite ferroelectric-remanence, which owns the poled state.

observed_text: Above the Curie point each crystallite of a perovskite ceramic is cubic with no dipole moment: BaTiO3 120 °C (393 K), PZT5H 195 °C, PZT4 320 °C, PZT5A 365 °C. A ceramic can depole below it (187 °C against a Curie point of 325 °C in Na0.5Bi0.5TiO3). Quartz has a structural inversion at 573.3 °C.
implied_text: PZT fails as a large piezo at ferroelectric T_C even while a solid remains. Quartz fails only by losing the non-centrosymmetric grid.
description: Ferroelectric piezo has a T_C collapse of the large d_ij. Quartz does not share that cliff.
notes: value_si is BaTiO3. Depoling below Tc is a separate, gradual route (crossover). Whether β-quartz stays piezoelectric was not settled by an opened source.

observed_text: Melting or breakdown removes the lattice or the insulator. Short of that, a substrate clamps a film (AlN 1.8 pm/V clamped against 5.6 pm/V in the free crystal) and quartz d11 falls 11 % between −196 °C and 100 °C.
implied_text: No inversion-free solid, no linear d_ij. Shock-depoling or cracking is lattice damage, not a second copy of melting.
description: Melting or cracking destroys the strain–polarization hardware with the lattice.
value_text: melting / breakdown; clamping and temperature drift
notes: Cross-cite melting and dielectric-breakdown. The clamping and drift parts are continuous.

observed_text: With a centre of symmetry, or in class 432, every linear coefficient is zero.
implied_text: If inversion is a symmetry, the linear output is forbidden, independent of field strength short of breakdown.
description: Inversion present → d_ij = 0. As sharp a hardware condition as the plasma-frequency clock on reflection.
notes: Exact by symmetry.

observed_text: Of the 32 crystal classes 21 have no centre of symmetry and 20 of those are piezoelectric (class 432 is the exception). A centrosymmetric crystal of any size has no linear coupling. A ceramic needs a net poled direction.
implied_text: The hardware is an inversion-free grid. Size does not create d_ij if inversion is present. Polar memory of a poled ferroelectric is owned by ferroelectric-remanence.
description: The linear strain–polarization machine is provisioned only by a non-centrosymmetric lattice (20 of 32 classes).
notes: Corrected: the first version said 20 classes lack inversion. Electrostriction is quadratic and is not this entry.

observed_text: Plasma periods h/E: 0.28 fs (Al, 15.0 eV measured); 0.72 fs (Na, 5.75 eV); 1.1 fs (K, 3.80 eV); Ag 0.46 fs at the free-electron 9.0 eV and 1.1 fs at the measured 3.8 eV. Ionosphere: 1.1 µs at 1e10, 0.35 µs at 1e11, 0.11 µs at 1e12 m^-3.
implied_text: The collective cycle is the plasma period. A drive slower than that is returned; a faster one is not.
description: Clock is load-bearing. The metal cycle is 0.28–1.1 fs; the ionospheric cycle 0.1–1 µs.
notes: value_si is the geometric mean of the metal range. The first version gave the ionospheric cycle as microseconds.

observed_text: ωp = √(ne²/ε₀m) gives 15.8 eV for Al and 6.04 eV for Na against measured 15.0–15.3 and 5.75 eV, and lies 13–18 % above the measured value in K, Rb and Cs. For Ag it gives 8.99 eV against a measured 3.78 eV.
implied_text: QSA takes the measured edge as the clock specification. It does not derive the period from a more primitive node update, and the free-electron formula needs a material-specific screening correction.
description: Same class of gap as reflection taking λ/4πk as the decay length. Not a contradiction.
value_text: edge taken, not derived; ωp(n) needs a screening correction
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Contrast photoelectric-threshold: collective carrier density against a single-electron work function.

observed_text: Below the edge the metal reflects: a fresh aluminised mirror measures 90.0–91.4 % at 404–624 nm. Above it the alkalis transmit; Ag has a narrow transmission window near 320 nm and is otherwise absorbing.
implied_text: A material-typical plasma or interband edge: high R below, a propagating or absorbed wave above, at zero extra power.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits a spectral gate, not a stored state.
notes: Bound-charge analogue of ω≫ωp is refraction-dielectric’s ε→1 X-ray limit.

observed_text: Operating condition is a drive below the measured edge: Al 15.0–15.3 eV; Na 5.75 eV; K 3.80 eV; Ag 3.78–3.92 eV. No continuous external power beyond the incident field.
implied_text: Driven collective response, not a memory. ℏωp is an energy scale of the clock, not an activation barrier that holds a state.
description: The window is a clock ceiling, not a latch barrier.
value_text: drive below the edge (Ag: below 3.8–3.9 eV); no latch
notes: Do not identify the Ag edge at 3.8–3.9 eV with the Ag work function, 4.26–4.74 eV (photoelectric-threshold).

observed_text: Reflectance falls above the measured plasmon energy: Al 15.0–15.3 eV (82.7–81.0 nm); Na 5.75 eV; K 3.80 eV. Alkali films become transparent at Cs 440, Rb 360, K 315 and Na 210 nm. Ag: bulk R falls from 95.6 % at 381.5 nm to 5.5 % at 320.4 nm, with a transmission window near 320 nm that interband absorption closes by 301 nm.
implied_text: Drive faster than the collective screening clock and the reflected beam is lost. In a real metal the edge is steep and continuous, with a width set by damping and interband transitions; above it Ag absorbs.
description: This entry owns the spectral edge that reflection also lists. A crossover in a real metal; sharp only in the collisionless model.
value_text: above the edge: Al 15.0–15.3 eV; Ag 3.78–3.92 eV
notes: value_si is the Al plasmon energy over h. Al and Na lie 3–5 % below the free-electron value, K, Rb and Cs 13–18 % below, and Ag at 0.42 of it.

observed_text: Ionospheric peak densities of 1e10 to more than 1e12 m^-3 give plasma frequencies of 1 to more than 9 MHz (0.90, 2.84 and 8.98 MHz at 1e10, 1e11 and 1e12 m^-3). Radio below the plasma frequency of a layer is returned and higher frequencies pass; Faraday rotation is still measured at 100–200 MHz.
implied_text: The same gate in a dilute charged gas: in the collisionless model a wave below f_p does not propagate.
description: The ionosphere is the low-density instance of the same clock failure, and the filed case nearest the collisionless limit.
value_text: f below 1 to above 9 MHz is returned (ionosphere)
notes: value_si is the plasma frequency at 1e12 m^-3. The threshold label rests on the collisionless model; no measured width of the cutoff was opened.

observed_text: No thickness cutoff accompanies the spectral edge. A continuous 5.66 nm Au film transmits as the bulk-constant calculation predicts, and seeded Au is optically a continuous metal down to 1 nm. Carrier densities that set the edge: Al 1.81e29, Ag 5.86e28, Na 2.65e28 m^-3.
implied_text: The edge is a property of the carrier population and its density. No minimum film thickness is measured; the thickness dependence is a crossover owned by reflection.
description: The spectral edge needs a carrier population, not a minimum connected thickness.
value_text: no minimum thickness measured (continuous Au responds at 5.66 nm and at 1 nm)
notes: The first version carried a 10–20 nm floor and a 5–10 nm cliff inherited from reflection; both withdrawn. The key name is kept for stability.

observed_text: Ionospheric peak layer densities vary between 1e4 and more than 1e6 electrons per cm³ (1e10 to more than 1e12 m^-3), a factor of 5.9e16 to 1.8e18 below the carrier density of Ag or Al.
implied_text: The same clock rule runs in a dilute free-electron column. The hardware is a carrier density that sets a radio-band plasma frequency, not a crystal.
description: Dilute-plasma hardware is a charged column at 1e10–1e12 m^-3, not a metallic film.
notes: value_si is the geometric mean of the quoted range. The first version gave the ratio to a metal as about 1e17.

observed_text: Temperature change of the crystal over hundreds of seconds: heated to 130 °C over 350 s, neutron emission lasting about 120 s per cycle. Fusion in the target is prompt.
implied_text: Clock is the thermal cycle of the crystal, not τμ.
description: Thermal-cycle clock of order 100 s.
notes: Corrected from 'seconds' (Geuther et al. 2006).

observed_text: No muon is present in either published experiment. A pulsed-coil hydride has no such accelerator.
implied_text: Do not identify with μCF or with the EM-LENR cell.
description: Polar-field beam gate, not a latch and not μCF.
value_text: not μCF; not the hydride cell

observed_text: 2.45 MeV D–D neutrons, 1e4–1e5 per thermal cycle (about 10,500 in the two-crystal replication; 85,000 emitted in the first report), about 1,000 per second, about 4e-8 per accelerated ion. The neutron branch returns about 1e-6 of the beam power.
implied_text: Yield depends on tip, pressure and crystal size. Witness is the 2.45 MeV neutron.
description: D–D neutron burst per ramp.
notes: Lower bound of 1e3 dropped: no source. Not a power source (stated by the authors).

observed_text: Deuteron beam above 100 keV and 4 nA from one crystal (potential below 110 kV); 200 kV with two crystals. The D–D cross-section is effectively zero below 20 keV and 16.3 mb at 100 keV.
implied_text: Two stages in series: pyroelectric potential, then the ordinary D–D barrier.
description: A ~100 kV pyroelectric potential puts deuterons where the D–D cross-section is millibarns.

observed_text: No temperature change gives no pyroelectric charge and no field; no deuterium gives no D–D neutrons. Emission stops at once when the face discharges (X-ray rate from 4,000 per second to zero). No neutrons were observed below 0.7 mTorr or with a blunt tip.
implied_text: Missing field source or missing D closes the channel.
description: No temperature change, no D, or a discharge ends the output.
value_text: no ΔT, no D, or discharge

observed_text: A LiTaO3 crystal about 10 mm thick and 20–30 mm across, a 70 nm tungsten tip on its face, deuterium gas near 1 mTorr and a deuterated solid target. A 600 nm tip or no tip gave no measurable neutrons. The nuclear event is beam-target D–D.
implied_text: Polar crystal is the field source; the tip ionizes the gas; D is the fuel. No muon is present.
description: Pyroelectric crystal, sharp tip, D2 gas and deuterated target are the hardware.
notes: Sourced 2026-11-14. Published device: Naranjo et al. 2005; Geuther et al. 2006.

observed_text: The cyclotron frequency ωc = eB/m is the field-set clock. ħωc is the Landau-level spacing. The Hall plateau is not itself a radiated frequency; it is a DC resistance that remains stable while that clock keeps the Landau ladder resolved against scattering and against kT.
implied_text: The same eB/m combination that cyclotron-resonance reads as an absorption line is here the clock that keeps the gap resolved so a DC plateau can exist.
description: QHE runs on a cyclotron clock; the output is a resistance plateau, not an absorption line.
notes: Cross-cite cyclotron-resonance, which owns the line.

observed_text: QSA takes RH = h/νe² from metrology. Filling ν = ns h/(eB) is bookkeeping, not a derivation of why RH equals that combination. Bulk gap plus edge path is the measured surviving hardware.
implied_text: QSA does not obtain h/e² from a node-count or buffer rule, and it does not yet specify why current is expelled to the edge and why that forces RH onto RK/ν. Fractional plateaus are explicitly unmapped.
description: The quantized Hall resistance is a universal output taken from metrology, not derived from node rules. That missing derivation is load-bearing.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Same class of gap as taking δ = λ/4πk as the mirror thickness, but here the output is a universal constant. No anyon or fractional-charge story is added.

observed_text: Quantized Hall resistance at integer plateaus: RH = h/(ν e²) = RK/ν, with the von Klitzing constant RK = h/e² ≈ 25812.807 Ω. On a plateau, Rxx → 0.
implied_text: A Hall resistance locked to RK/ν together with a vanishing longitudinal resistance, while the 2DEG, the perpendicular field, the temperature, and the current remain inside the envelope.
description: The stable metrological output is RH = h/νe² with Rxx → 0.
notes: Complementary lock to josephson-effect (2e/h). Fractional plateaus are a harder related case and are not the primary artifact.

observed_text: Plateaus survive only while kT and the Hall electric field remain small compared with the gap that the Landau-level spacing (plus the sample's disorder-broadened mobility gap) sets. Graphene in a large perpendicular field can still show integer plateaus near room temperature — the same gap-versus-kT constraint.
implied_text: The Landau-level (mobility) gap is the energy barrier that protects a plateau. The perpendicular-field condition is a field threshold that opens the gap; moving B so that ν sits between integers takes the system out of a gap.
description: A plateau is a gap-protected DC state: kT or a Hall field comparable to the gap collapses the quantization.
notes: Disorder that widens a plateau is a sample-dependent resource, analogous to pinning on type-ii-critical-field. Integer values of RH do not depend on closing it; the width of the flat region does.

observed_text: An in-plane field does not open this artifact. The field must be perpendicular to the plane.
implied_text: Wrong field orientation is a hardware-gate failure: the Landau ladder of this machine does not open.
description: In-plane B is a non-occurrence of the integer quantum Hall machine.
notes: Distinct from moving a perpendicular B off a plateau.

observed_text: Moving the field off a plateau destroys the flatness and restores a finite Rxx. Off the plateau, Rxx is finite and RH is not flat. Plateaus are centred where ν = ns h/(eB) sits near an integer.
implied_text: When ν is not in a gap, the protected edge-channel output is gone.
description: Off-integer filling is the field/filling collapse of the plateau.
notes: Filling ν = ns h/(eB) locates the plateaus; it is bookkeeping, not a derivation of RH = h/νe².

observed_text: Low temperature and modest current are required; raising either washes the plateaus out. The precise current and temperature at which a given sample leaves metrological flatness are medium (mobility- and geometry-dependent). Destroying the 2DEG (density or mobility collapsed) removes the integer ladder.
implied_text: Thermal population of adjacent levels, or Hall-field / current breakdown, collapses the gap protection. Buffer destruction is a coarser failure of the same machine.
description: High T or high current wash the plateaus out by overrunning the Landau/mobility gap.
value_text: kT or Hall field vs gap
notes: Graphene's high-temperature integer plateaus sit on the same gap-versus-kT clause and do not require a second family.

observed_text: Hardware window: a 2D electron system (Si inversion layer, GaAs/AlGaAs heterojunction, later graphene) plus a magnetic field perpendicular to the plane. A bulk 3D metal in the same B does not produce these plateaus. An in-plane field does not open this artifact.
implied_text: A two-dimensional electron buffer plus a perpendicular field is the measured architecture. Once the field opens a gap in the bulk of the 2DEG, the surviving current path is along the edges. QSA records this layered hardware; it does not derive the edge path from node rules.
description: Integer quantum Hall plateaus need a 2DEG and a perpendicular field; a 3D metal is the wrong buffer.
notes: Magnetic length ℓB = √(ℏ/eB) is the in-plane spatial scale set by B; no universal nanometre number is quoted.

observed_text: Fermi-velocity transit through the saddle. The staircase is DC.
implied_text: Not a cyclotron clock and not a Hall plateau clock.
description: Transit clock; DC output.

observed_text: No perpendicular B is required. Output is two-terminal 2e²/h, not Hall h/νe². The 0.7 feature is out of scope.
implied_text: Do not mint a tenth design that swallows QHE and QPC.
description: QPC is not QHE. 2e²/h is taken.

observed_text: G = n × 2e²/h with 2e²/h ≈ 7.748e-5 S.
implied_text: Taken Landauer output. Not RH = h/νe².
description: Two-terminal conductance steps at 2e²/h.

observed_text: 1D subband edges open one by one. Pinch-off closes the last mode. No pairing gap and no Landau gap.
implied_text: Subband edges are the gates.
description: Mode edges, not 2Δ and not ħωc.

observed_text: Pinch-off gives G→0. High T or a dirty/long channel washes the steps.
implied_text: Last-mode close, thermal smear, or lost ballistic buffer collapse the staircase.
description: Pinch-off / T / mfp are the collapses.

observed_text: Ballistic constriction of width ~ λF (tens of nm in a GaAs 2DEG), shorter than the mfp. No perpendicular B required.
implied_text: 1D saddle in a 2DEG is the buffer. A wide 3D metal is the wrong hardware.
description: QPC needs a ballistic ~λF constriction.

observed_text: Plasma periods h/E: 0.28 fs at the measured Al plasmon (15.0 eV); 0.46 fs at the free-electron model value for Ag (9.0 eV); 1.1 fs at the measured Ag plasmon (3.8 eV). A photoemission delay of about 100 as, measured on tungsten, is of the same order.
implied_text: Collective screening and the phase-reversed re-radiation complete on the plasma-period timescale.
description: The electron population responds within a few 10^-16 to 10^-15 s; the image is complete on any macroscopic clock. The data do not separate a faster single-electron step from it.
notes: The first version cited attosecond streaking as a faster single-electron step in these metals; the measurement was on tungsten and is 1e-16 s. value_si lies between the Al and the Ag free-electron periods.

observed_text: The decay length is δ = λ/4πk (Ag 12–15 nm, Al 6.6–8.3 nm at 450–650 nm), and k is itself an optical constant of the same electrons.
implied_text: QSA takes the measured decay length; it does not derive it from a more primitive node count. It is a decay scale, not a buffer minimum.
description: The decay length is located but not derived from node rules. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping lowered from High to Medium on 2026-11-12.

observed_text: Bulk R computed from tabulated n and k at 450–650 nm: Ag 97.3–99.0 % in the measured sets and 91.9–96.5 % in the fits; Al 90.4–92.4 %. A fresh aluminised mirror measures 90.0–91.4 % at 404–624 nm. No continuous external power to the metal beyond the incident field.
implied_text: Stable phase-reversed reflected beam with material-typical R(λ), at zero extra power.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits a macroscopic reflected beam without a hold-power budget.
notes: The reflectance of polished Ag was not read from a mirror measurement. value_si is Ag at 550 nm.

observed_text: No continuous external power is required to maintain the reflected image beyond the incident field itself.
implied_text: Hold-power of the mirror is zero; the drive is the light being reflected.
description: The mirror is not a powered lamp. Continuous draw to hold R is zero.

observed_text: Operating window is a drive frequency below the plasma edge (Al) or the interband-screened edge (Ag, 3.8–3.9 eV). No thickness condition is measured: reflectance scales continuously with thickness.
implied_text: This is a driven collective response, not a memory. There is no static barrier holding a latched state.
description: Reflection has an operating condition on drive frequency, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
value_text: ω below the edge (Al 15.0 eV; Ag 3.8–3.9 eV); no thickness condition
notes: Negative latch spec: contrast with permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: Reflectance falls at the plasma or interband edge. Al plasmon 15.0 eV (measured). Ag: bulk R computed from tabulated n and k falls from 95.6 % at 381.5 nm to 5.5 % at 320.4 nm (3.87 eV); the measured plasmon is at 3.8 eV against a free-electron model value of 9 eV.
implied_text: Drive faster than the collective screening clock and the reflected beam is lost. In a real metal the edge has a width set by damping and interband transitions; a sharp cutoff belongs to the collisionless model.
description: The same population that reflects below the edge stops reflecting above it. Owned by plasma-frequency-cutoff.
value_text: above the edge: Al 15.0 eV; Ag 3.8–3.9 eV (model 9 eV)
notes: Cross-cite plasma-frequency-cutoff, which owns this edge. value_si is the Al plasmon energy over h.

observed_text: Single-layer Fresnel calculation with bulk constants at 550 nm. Free-standing Ag: R = 13.6 % at 5 nm, 38.9 % at 10 nm, 73.8 % at 20 nm, 96.4 % at 50 nm. Al: 41–50 % at 5 nm, 68–74 % at 10 nm. A continuous 5.66 nm Au film matches the same calculation; thinner Au transmits less than the ideal film. Percolation (6–7 nm unseeded Au, 6–12 nm unseeded Ag, 1–3 nm on a copper seed) is abrupt in dc conductance and monotonic in the optical response.
implied_text: Thinning lowers the output continuously because less responding material is traversed. No thickness switches the mirror off; islanding removes dc conduction, not the optical response.
description: Thickness is a crossover: transmitted intensity falls as exp(−d/δ) with δ = λ/4πk, and half of bulk R is a convention.
value_text: half of bulk R at 12–14 nm (Ag), 4.5–6 nm (Al), 550 nm
notes: The first version called this a collapse below 5–10 nm. Morphology is a threshold in dc conductance only (Hövel 2010). value_si is the half-reflectance thickness of free-standing Ag.

observed_text: Intensity e-folding length λ/4πk at 450–650 nm, computed from tabulated n and k: Ag 11.6–15.4 nm, Al 6.6–8.3 nm. Reflectance of a continuous film rises smoothly with thickness: half of bulk R at 12–14 nm (Ag) and 4.5–6 nm (Al) at 550 nm. A collective optical response is measured at one atomic layer (graphene, 2.3 % absorption), at 1.65 nm of Ag(111), at 1 nm of seeded Au and in 2 nm particles.
implied_text: No minimum connected buffer is measured. The response scales with how much responding metal the field passes through; λ/4πk (49–65 planes of Ag, 28–36 of Al) is the decay scale of a continuous curve, not a threshold.
description: Reflection has no measured minimum thickness. Reflectance grows continuously with the metal traversed, on the scale of the decay length λ/4πk.
value_text: δ = λ/4πk: Ag 12–15 nm (49–65 planes), Al 6.6–8.3 nm (28–36 planes); a decay length, not a minimum
notes: The first version read 10–20 nm (40–85 planes) as a minimum connected buffer; withdrawn. The key name is kept for stability. value_si is the Ag decay length at 550 nm.

observed_text: Optical period λ/c is 1.50 fs at 450 nm, 1.83 fs at 550 nm and 2.17 fs at 650 nm. Water has a static dielectric constant of 80.10 at 20 °C and an optical permittivity n² = 1.7778.
implied_text: The bound-charge population must track the optical cycle. Channels slower than the drive fall out of the synchronized response. Drive well above the electronic resonances leaves n≈1.
description: Visible electronic refraction completes on a 1.5–2.2 fs cycle; a slower polarization channel is already off the clock.
notes: Water is the split-channel example: static 80.10 (20 °C) against optical 1.7778. The assignment of the difference to orientational polarization was not checked against an opened source.

observed_text: Clausius–Mossotti / Lorentz–Lorenz relate (ε_r−1)/(ε_r+2) and (n²−1)/(n²+2) to Nα. They do not derive α from node rules. No thickness is measured at which refraction appears.
implied_text: QSA takes tabulated n(ω) and the X-ray δ as the contrast specification.
description: Contrast is located as Nα but α is not derived. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping remains Medium. No source for the two relations was opened in the 2026-11 pass.

observed_text: At 589.3 nm, from fitted dispersion formulas: water (20.0 °C) 1.33335; fused silica 1.45840; N-BK7 crown glass 1.51673; diamond 2.4173; standard dry air 1.000277. Optical permittivity is n².
implied_text: A stable, material- and frequency-specific n(ω) and the macroscopic Snell kink from synchronized bound-charge polarization.
description: The synchronized bound-charge population emits a tabulated n(ω) and a ray bend.
notes: value_si is N-BK7 crown glass. total-internal-reflection is the geometry/index gate on this same n.

observed_text: The dielectric itself draws no continuous power.
implied_text: Hold-power of the refracting slab is zero; the drive is the incident field.
description: Continuous draw to hold n is zero.

observed_text: Zero continuous power and no stored directional state. Dielectric strength from a handbook compilation: air 3 MV/m; solids from 9.8–13.8 MV/m (window glass) to 470–670 MV/m (fused silica) and 2000 MV/m (diamond). Breakdown ends the insulating window.
implied_text: Driven collective response, not a memory. The high-field edge is a different machine class (dielectric-breakdown), not a sharper location of n.
description: Refraction has an operating window, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
value_text: no latch; Ebd is a different family
notes: Cross-cite dielectric-breakdown. Do not file breakdown as the refraction cliff. The strengths rest on a tertiary page; the first version gave solids as 1e7–1e8 V/m.

observed_text: Above the electronic response the index is n = 1 − δ, with δ = n_e r_e λ²/2π in the free-electron limit: Si 5.4e-5 at 3 keV, 7.4e-6 at 8.05 keV, 1.2e-6 at 20 keV; water 2.6e-5, 3.6e-6, 5.8e-7. Vacuum is N = 0. n1 = n2 gives no interface kink.
implied_text: ε→1 (X-ray, vacuum, or drive above the electronic response) removes the contrast continuously and the ray kink fades.
description: The spectral and density failure is n−1→0, a crossover that goes as δ ∝ n_e λ².
value_text: δ ~ 1e-6–1e-5 at about 8–20 keV (light solids); n−1→0
notes: value_si is the geometric mean of the quoted δ decade. The first version placed that decade at a few keV. The δ values are this file's free-electron estimate. X-ray n<1 grazing total external reflection is the same kinematic gate as TIR with inverted contrast; geometry owned by total-internal-reflection. Free-electron analogue is plasma-frequency-cutoff.

observed_text: The phase 2π(n−1)d/λ is proportional to the path d. A path much shorter than λ gives a fringe-level shift, not a resolvable ray.
implied_text: A short path gives a proportionally small output. 'A wavelength or more' is a convention for calling the result a ray.
description: A short path is a continuous reduction of the ray output, not a missing polarizable volume.

observed_text: A slab of thickness d adds a phase 2π(n−1)d/λ relative to vacuum, proportional to d. No thickness marks a beginning of refraction.
implied_text: Hardware is a polarizable bound-charge volume and a path through it; the output grows with the material traversed. Vacuum (N=0) and X-ray δ→0 are the low-contrast end of the same resource.
description: Refraction has no minimum thickness. The phase accumulates in proportion to (n−1) times the path.
notes: The first version contrasted this with a 10–20 nm metal-mirror floor, which does not exist. Reflection and refraction now agree that the output scales with the thickness traversed.

observed_text: The optical cycle and the interband polarization response sit in the femtosecond neighbourhood of visible / near-IR light.
implied_text: Relative to any laboratory shutter the conversion, when allowed, is already complete.
description: Interband conversion latency sits in the femtosecond optical-cycle neighbourhood.

observed_text: Indirect-gap edges (Si, Ge, diamond) rise more slowly: the conversion also consumes or emits a phonon. Direct gaps (GaAs) open with the photon alone.
implied_text: Indirect conversion needs a lattice-clock resource just above threshold. That is an extra resource on the same Eg gate, not a second family.
description: The slower rise of α in Si and Ge is a phonon-clock requirement, not a different collapse energy.
notes: No ħω_ph number is given. A frozen lattice with no phonon occupancy would starve the indirect channel at threshold.

observed_text: QSA here takes the measured Eg as the specification. Urbach tails and excitons are recorded as measured softness, not extra mechanisms.
implied_text: No derivation of why a given crystal has the gap it has from node rules alone. The collapse hν < Eg does not depend on that derivation.
description: The gate is located; its value is not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step.

observed_text: A material-typical absorption edge and the associated split between a transmitting window and an opaque band. Ordinary wafers are optically thick in the visible once above Eg.
implied_text: Stable spectral split — window below Eg, opacity above — whenever a photon population is presented to an intact gapped lattice.
description: The machine’s stable product is a crystal-typical absorption edge, not a stored state.

observed_text: Room-temperature gaps (300 K): Si Eg ≈ 1.12 eV (indirect); Ge ≈ 0.66 eV; GaAs ≈ 1.42 eV (direct); diamond ~5.5 eV.
implied_text: Eg is the load-bearing gate. Direct gaps open with the photon alone; indirect with photon plus phonon. Temperature moves Eg; it does not replace it.
description: Gap absorption is a photoelectric-class energy gate relocated into a bulk crystal.
value_text: Si Eg ≈ 1.12 eV (300 K); Ge 0.66; GaAs 1.42; diamond ~5.5
notes: value_si is Si at 300 K. Photoconductivity must share this collapse energy. Low-T limits sit higher by tens to ~100 meV.

observed_text: The edge is a property of the intact crystal: melting or amorphizing the lattice destroys the sharp crystalline edge.
implied_text: Loss of crystalline order washes the sharp edge into a smeared amorphous spectrum.
description: Destroy the periodic grid and the gate’s sharp location goes with it. Lattice-resource failure, not a change of family.

observed_text: Below Eg the crystal has a transparency window. Below-threshold light is refracted and, at most, weakly attenuated by processes that are not interband conversion.
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below Eg the interband gate stays shut.
notes: Urbach tails and excitons are softness of the same gate, not a second channel. Free-carrier/impurity absorption can hide the window without opening this conversion.

observed_text: The gate is a property of the periodic lattice: a filled valence band and an empty conduction band separated by Eg. A single unit cell already carries the gap; macroscopic opacity is the summed conversion over an optical path of order 1/α.
implied_text: Hardware is a gapped lattice, not a surface φ and not a collective optical buffer. Destroying crystalline order removes the sharp edge.
description: One unit cell carries Eg. Path length sets how much light is converted, not whether the gate exists.
notes: No numerical 1/α is given; do not invent an absorption length.

observed_text: Precession scale γ/2π = 28.025 GHz/T (CODATA 2022). Elongated iron particles of 130–305 Å reverse by a non-coherent mode closest to chain-of-spheres fanning; alnico rods of 40–50 nm start to reverse by curling.
implied_text: Geometry changes the barrier and leaves the carrier unchanged. Write latency is set by the field sweep and by the reversal mode.
description: The shape latch uses the same 28 GHz/T precession clock as the crystal-K1 latch.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency. The first version listed curling and buckling and omitted fanning.

observed_text: The coercive force predicted for shape anisotropy frequently far exceeds the observed value. Elongated iron reaches 1600–2000 Oe, 15–19 % of the 10.7 kOe of an ideal needle, and reverses by fanning. Alnico rods exceed the coherent diameter, start to reverse by curling and do not reach the Stoner–Wohlfarth limit.
implied_text: ΔN does not predict the measured switching field; this is the same mesoscale Hc gap as on the hysteresis file. The continuous zero of ΔN at aspect ratio 1 does not depend on closing it.
description: Switching-field numbers remain mesoscale: measured values are 15–19 % of the ideal-ellipsoid field.
value_text: H_c ≈ 0.15–0.19 of the ideal needle field (Fe)
notes: File-level mapping was lowered from High to Medium for this reason. This entry owns the ΔN term only; shape and crystal anisotropy add when both are present.

observed_text: Elongated iron particles (150 Å, 3:1) have an intrinsic coercive force of 1600 Oe, and coercive force correlates with elongation; bulk polycrystalline iron has 10–100 A/m. A film magnetizes perpendicular to its plane only when K > μ0Ms²/2; CoFeB/MgO is perpendicular up to a CoFeB thickness of 1.5 nm.
implied_text: Stable output is a uniaxial remanent direction locked to the long axis of a particle, or to the plane of a film, without a large magnetocrystalline K1.
description: The geometry barrier emits long-axis (or in-plane) remanence at zero hold-power.
value_text: M locked to long axis / film plane
notes: 1600 Oe is 127 kA/m. In CoFeB/MgO the reorientation is a threshold at a system-specific thickness of about 1.2–1.5 nm.

observed_text: Holding the long-axis remanent state costs zero continuous power: it is a static configuration, and no source reports a dissipation at rest.
implied_text: Stable long-axis remanence at zero continuous power, without a large K1.
description: Holding the shape latch costs zero watts.

observed_text: Kshape = (μ0/2)Ms²ΔN. The scale (μ0/2)Ms² is 1.84 MJ/m³ in Fe (2.15 T) and 0.15 MJ/m³ in Ni. The needle maximum for Fe is 0.92 MJ/m³: 18 times iron's own K1 (0.05 MJ/m³), 4.7–5.3 times below Nd2Fe14B (4.3–4.9) and 19 times below SmCo5 (17.2). The maximum shape anisotropy gives a hardness parameter κ = 0.5.
implied_text: The barrier is magnetostatic and geometric. No large K1 is required, and the latch it supplies is semi-hard. Holding the long-axis remanent state costs zero continuous power.
description: Shape alone latches a high-Ms needle with a barrier of at most 0.92 MJ/m³ in Fe: 18 times iron's crystal K1 and 5 to 19 times below a rare-earth K1.
value_text: K_shape ≤ 0.92 MJ/m³ in Fe (0.44 at 2:1, 0.86 at 10:1); (μ0/2)Ms² = 1.84 MJ/m³
notes: value_si is the Fe needle maximum, half of (μ0/2)Ms². The first version said the Fe scale matched a hard-magnet K1 and that the Ni scale was several times smaller; it is 12 times smaller. Measured switching fields of elongated iron reach 15–19 % of the ideal needle field.

observed_text: ΔN of a prolate spheroid is 0.240 at aspect ratio 2, 0.416 at 5 and 0.470 at 10, against the needle limit 0.5 (48 %, 83 % and 94 % of it). It is zero at aspect ratio 1: a sphere has 1/3 on every axis.
implied_text: The geometry barrier scales with ΔN and goes to zero continuously as the body approaches a sphere, at any volume and any Ms.
description: ΔN falls continuously to zero as the aspect ratio approaches 1; half the needle limit is already reached near aspect ratio 2.
notes: A continuous zero; the first version called it a sharp collapse. Alnico sits on this file with a qualifier (rods thicker than the coherent diameter). Nd2Fe14B does not need shape: its K1 (4.3–4.9 MJ/m³) exceeds its magnetostatic scale (1.03 MJ/m³).

observed_text: The barrier goes as Ms² and vanishes with Ms at the Curie temperature: Fe 1044 K, Ni 628 K. μ0Ms is 2.15 T in Fe and 0.61–0.62 T in Ni, so the Ni scale is 12 times below the Fe scale.
implied_text: The geometry barrier is proportional to Ms². Lose the moment and the needle stops being a latch.
description: Shape anisotropy vanishes with Ms at the Curie point, and is smaller in proportion to Ms² in a weak-moment material.
value_text: μ0 M_s = 2.15 T (Fe); barrier ~ M_s^2; Tc 1044 K (Fe)
notes: The Curie point is the threshold. Between materials the dependence on Ms is continuous. The thermal volume limit is a crossover, filed as superparamagnetism with K = Kshape.

observed_text: The demagnetizing factors of a uniformly magnetized ellipsoid sum to 1. Sphere: 1/3 on every axis, so ΔN = 0. Infinite wire: 1/2, 1/2, 0. Thin film: 0, 0, 1. For a prolate spheroid ΔN is 0.240, 0.416 and 0.470 at aspect ratios 2, 5 and 10. Reversal is coherent only below a coherence radius of about five exchange lengths (7.4–16 nm in Fe, Co, Ni).
implied_text: The latch cell is a ferromagnetic particle or precipitate with nonzero ΔN, thinner than the coherent diameter and large enough to pass the thermal cut. A sphere has no geometry barrier at any size.
description: Shape latch hardware is an anisotropic body (needle or plate), not a unit cell and not a sphere.
notes: The demagnetizing factors are exact magnetostatics; the spheroid values are computed from Osborn's formula, whose paper was opened as an abstract only. Alnico rods of 40–50 nm exceed the coherent diameter of about 20 nm.

observed_text: Magnetic diffusivity D = ρ/μ0 is 0.0137 m²/s in IACS copper. Steady drive: δ ∝ f^(−1/2). Single pulse of length t: 2√(Dt) in the railgun literature and 0.8–2 times √(Dt) across rules (0.093–0.23 mm at 1 μs, 0.93–2.3 mm at 100 μs, 1.3–6.2 mm at 0.2–0.7 ms). Moving contact of length a at speed V: 2√(Da/V), which is 0.73 mm at 100 m/s and 0.33 mm at 500 m/s for a = 1 mm. The same electrons have a plasma period of 0.28–0.46 fs.
implied_text: The low-frequency clock is magnetic diffusion across the conductor, set by measured ρ and μ. One diffusivity is read against three drive clocks: period, elapsed time and transit time.
description: Skin is the same screening machine as reflection, run in the magnetic-diffusion band rather than on the plasma period.
value_text: 60 Hz class (power); δ ∝ f^(−1/2); pulse depth ∝ √(Dt) with D = 0.0137 m²/s (Cu)
notes: Cross-cite reflection (optical plasma period) and plasma-frequency-cutoff (high-frequency end). 60 Hz is an operating point, not a clock threshold. The pulse prefactor is a convention; the moving-contact depth is model-only, with no direct measurement found.

observed_text: QSA takes δ = √(2ρ/ωμ) as the buffer specification. The square root is the diffusion law with D = ρ/μ; that constant is measured and is not derived from a more primitive node count.
implied_text: The spatial buffer is located (classical δ, under a local Ohm's law) but not derived from node rules.
description: Same class of gap as reflection taking λ/4πk: the length is measured, then used as the hardware spec.
notes: File-level mapping remains High.

observed_text: AC current density is highest at the surface and falls as e^(−x/δ); a wire much thicker than δ has about the resistance of a hollow tube of wall δ carrying direct current. Neighbouring conductors redistribute the current further (proximity effect).
implied_text: Frequency-dependent concentration of AC current toward the surface, and the associated rise in AC resistance, from collective screening.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits an exponentially screened interior and a current sheet of 1/e depth δ.
notes: cyclotron-resonance (Azbel'–Kaner) uses this skin layer as the volume the microwave field occupies.

observed_text: The metal requires no auxiliary power beyond the current itself.
implied_text: Driven dissipative response, not a latch and not a gapped condensate. No static barrier holds the current distribution.
description: Skin has an operating window on ω and thickness, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
notes: Meissner replaces this dissipative layer with a static London depth — different family.

observed_text: The local relation J = σE fails when δ falls below the mean free path ℓ. Copper at 293 K: ℓ = 39–40 nm against δ = 3.56 μm at 340 MHz (ratio 91) and 1.0–2.5 mm at 0.7–4 kHz; δ would equal ℓ only near 3 THz. In the extreme limit the surface resistance goes from ω^(1/2) to ω^(2/3).
implied_text: Mean-free-path over-run takes the machine out of the classical-δ specification into a different operating length. It is not reached in room-temperature copper below the terahertz range.
description: Anomalous skin is a local-response failure of the classical buffer, approached continuously in ℓ/δ.
value_text: ℓ ≳ δ; Cu at 293 K: ℓ = 39–40 nm
notes: The δ ∝ ω^(−1/3) scaling is inferred from the surface-resistance exponent; no opened source states it. Cold copper with a residual resistivity ratio near 100 has ℓ of about 4 μm. Pippard (1947) and Reuter and Sondheimer (1948) were not opened. Keep classical, anomalous and optical lengths distinct.

observed_text: δ ∝ ω^(−1/2) grows without limit as ω → 0, and when δ is large against the conductor the current distribution is that of steady conduction. A factor of ten in frequency changes δ by a factor of about 3.
implied_text: Drive slower than the diffusion clock of the conductor → the surface-to-centre contrast fades continuously. There is no critical frequency.
description: The low-frequency collapse is uniform fill, reached continuously. Same machine as reflection, failed by a too-slow clock rather than a too-fast one.
notes: Twin of plasma-frequency-cutoff: that entry owns ω>ωp; this entry owns ω→0. The scale is δ = a.

observed_text: Field and current density fall as e^(−x/δ). A conductor whose half-thickness a ≪ δ carries current over its whole cross-section; a wire much thicker than δ has about the resistance of a tube of wall δ. At 4δ the amplitude is 1.8 % of the surface value.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning relative to δ: the responding population occupies the entire cross-section and the surface-to-centre contrast is absent.
description: The spatial twin of reflection’s thin-film limit, written against classical δ rather than optical λ/4πk. A crossover in a/δ.
notes: At 60 Hz in Cu the comparison length is 8.4–8.5 mm; at 1 GHz it is 2.1 μm. Cross-cite reflection for the optical thin-film limit.

observed_text: δ = √(ρ/(π f μ0 μr)) is the 1/e depth of an exponential profile with a phase lag of one radian per δ. Copper at 293 K (pure 1.678e-8 Ω·m to IACS 1.7241e-8 Ω·m): 8.4–8.5 mm at 60 Hz; 2.1 mm at 1 kHz; 65–66 μm at 1 MHz; 2.1 μm at 1 GHz.
implied_text: The buffer is the screening length δ, quoted at 1/e by convention. There is no minimum thickness: a conductor of half-thickness a shows a surface-to-centre contrast that grows with a/δ.
description: Skin hardware is thickness against δ(ω), a 1/e length. The same metal is millimetres at power frequency and micrometres at radio frequency.
value_text: δ = 8.4–8.5 mm (Cu, 60 Hz) … 2.1 μm (1 GHz); 1/e depth
notes: value_si is 60 Hz in pure copper; IACS copper gives 8.53 mm. Optical λ/4πk (Ag 12.8 nm, Al 6.6 nm as intensity depths) is owned by reflection; London λ by meissner. A single pulse and a moving contact have their own depths (see the clock row). Do not collapse the lengths.

observed_text: Dry air at 0 °C: 331.46 ± 0.10 m s⁻¹; at 20 °C and 10 % humidity 343.5 m s⁻¹. Distilled water at 20 °C: 1482.36 m s⁻¹. Mild steel: 5960 m s⁻¹ bulk longitudinal, 5196 rod, 3235 shear. Copper 4759 and 2325; aluminium 6374 and 3111 m s⁻¹.
implied_text: The long-wave clock speed is the q→0 slope of the acoustic branch on the same grid phonon-dispersion maps at finite q. No single v_s is universal.
description: Sound speed is the material-typical √(C/ρ) slope, not a universal constant.
value_text: air 343.5 m/s (20 °C); water 1482 m/s; mild steel 5960 / 3235 m/s
notes: value_si left null: examples, not one pin. Speeds computed from K, G and density agree with the measured ones within 0.3 % for Cu, Al, Ni. Polyatomic gases disperse near a relaxation frequency (CO₂ 280 → 293 m/s).

observed_text: Transit time on a path L is t = L/v_s. Computed: 5 m of air 14.6 ms; 5 m of steel rod 0.96 ms; 5 cm of steel rod 9.6 µs.
implied_text: The macroscopic acoustic clock is the transit L/v_s and the period λ/v_s, not the Debye ceiling.
description: A laboratory path is about 15 ms in air and about 1 ms in steel over 5 m; microseconds apply to centimetres of metal.
value_text: t = L/v_s; 14.6 ms (5 m air); 0.96 ms (5 m steel rod)
notes: Corrected: the first version gave microseconds for a metal bar of room length.

observed_text: A closed mapping would say why a given solid has the C it has, from node-spring rules, rather than taking handbook moduli as input. The speed measurement does not depend on closing it.
implied_text: QSA takes measured C and ρ and reads v_s = √(C/ρ). It does not derive the moduli from node springs.
description: The slope is located; the springs that set C are not derived here. Same gap as elasticity.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Ideal-gas air and condensed water share the Newton–Laplace form on different hardware; ideal-gas-pressure owns the wall force, not this slope.

observed_text: A pair {v_L, v_T} in a solid or a single speed in a fluid, fixed by modulus and density. Examples: air 343.5 m s⁻¹ at 20 °C; water 1482 m s⁻¹; mild steel 5960 and 3235 m s⁻¹; copper 4759 and 2325 m s⁻¹.
implied_text: The synchronized long-wavelength output of the coupled mechanical population is that material-typical slope set.
description: The machine emits a handbook v_s class, not one universal speed.
value_text: {v_L, v_T} solid; v_L fluid (air 343.5; water 1482; steel 5960 / 3235 m/s)
notes: Same springs as elasticity, read as a slope. qa ~ 1 moves the mode onto the phonon-dispersion curve.

observed_text: The operating condition is a finite restoring modulus (bulk, and shear if a shear wave is claimed) plus a density. The wave is a launched collective oscillation, not a memory.
implied_text: No latched barrier. Presence of C and ρ provisions the slope; holding a sound field is not a zero-power memory.
description: Sound is a driven collective oscillation of coupled nodes, not a stored directional state.
value_text: finite C and ρ; no latch

observed_text: Liquids are tabulated with one compressional speed (liquid tin 2471 m s⁻¹ at 240 °C, liquid zinc 2780 at 450 °C). On melting the static shear modulus goes from a finite value to zero. Liquid gallium carries transverse excitations only above a wavevector of 9 nm⁻¹, with a lifetime of 0.5 ps and a range of 0.4–0.5 nm.
implied_text: G = 0 at acoustic frequencies means the shear restoring coupling is absent in the liquid. The compressional wave remains. At picosecond periods a liquid still responds transversely over a few atomic spacings.
description: No static shear modulus, no shear sound wave. Melting removes the solid's shear wave in a jump.
value_text: G = 0 in the liquid at acoustic frequencies; shear wave lost at T_m
notes: Cross-cite melting. The exception at THz frequency is a crossover in frequency, filed in the effect file.

observed_text: A vacuum has no coupled mechanical medium: no wave is launched and v_s is undefined there.
implied_text: No nodes, no wave. Vacuum is missing hardware, not a limiting speed of zero.
description: Sound dies when the coupled medium is absent. v_s is undefined in vacuum.

observed_text: The continuum speed holds for wavelengths long against the node spacing. A vacuum has no medium. Liquids are tabulated with one compressional speed; solids with a longitudinal and a shear speed.
implied_text: Hardware is a coupled mechanical population with many nodes per wavelength, plus the relevant restoring modulus.
description: Sound requires a medium and the modulus that provisions the claimed branch. Vacuum has no nodes; fluids do not provision shear.

observed_text: No separate clock beyond the wall-equilibration window and the spectral content already fixed by kT/h. The T^4 law is a time-averaged power.
implied_text: A detector faster than the wall exchange, or a surface whose T is not itself stable, does not report σT^4.
description: The T^4 reading inherits the wall averaging window and the spectral clock of the Planck curve.
notes: Clock inherited from blackbody-spectrum and thermal-equilibrium-temperature. k and h are defined.

observed_text: σ = 2π^5 k^4/(15 c^2 h^3) is a combination of defined constants. Finite-size corrections confirm that area and λ_max are the spatial resources and do not yield a single universal area.
implied_text: The mapping’s job is the T^4 envelope and its failures, not a re-derivation of the prefactor.
description: σ is defined; no universal radiating area is extracted. That is inherited from the spectrum entry.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Thermionic emission from the same hot surface is a charged-particle gate, not this photon-current integral.

observed_text: A hot black surface radiates a hemispherical exitance j = εσT^4. Doubling T multiplies the exitance by sixteen.
implied_text: The T^4 exitance is the power-meter reading of a black thermal surface — the frequency integral of the Planck curve.
description: Relabel the T^4 law as the integrated output of the thermal electromagnetic population. The prefactor is not a QSA extraction.
notes: σ = 5.670374e-8 W m^{-2} K^{-4} is defined from h, k, and c. Extracting σ as an independent machine constant would double-count those defined constants.

observed_text: None holding a latched state. A high-reflectivity metal is a resource failure of the black boundary condition (ε collapsed), not a stored configuration.
implied_text: Low ε is not a memory. The operating condition is a black (or grey) surface, not a barrier.
description: Stefan–Boltzmann has a black-boundary operating condition, not an energy barrier that stores a state.
notes: Cross-cite reflection.

observed_text: Surface not black (ε(ν)≠1 across the Wien band) → reduced or non-T^4 output. A grey surface still follows T^4 with a reduced prefactor; a selective surface does not.
implied_text: The extra collapse of the integral is a boundary-condition failure of the same electromagnetic population, not a new machine.
description: Non-black or selective surfaces take the power meter off σT^4.
notes: The same surface can be nearly black in the thermal infrared and reflective in the visible.

observed_text: Object or cavity not large compared with λ_max(T), or modes under-populated → the integral of a non-Planck spectrum is not σT^4. Finite-size / diffraction corrections appear in that regime.
implied_text: Area and λ_max are the spatial resources of the integral, for the same reason a sparse cavity leaves the Planck curve.
description: Undersized radiators fall off the T^4 envelope.
notes: Cross-cite blackbody-spectrum. No universal area is attached.

observed_text: As T→0 the radiated power vanishes into the instrument floor. Net exchange between two black surfaces is σ(T1^4−T2^4).
implied_text: Shrink the thermal resource and the photon current disappears. An undefined wall T is the same inherited collapse as the temperature entry.
description: T→0, or an unstable wall T, kills the T^4 reading.
notes: At 300 K, σT^4 ≈ 459 W m^{-2} is arithmetic from defined σ, not a machine number.

observed_text: The surface must present ε≈1 across the Wien band, and the radiating object must be large compared with λ_max(T), or the output is not σT^4. There is no single universal size cliff; the required area tracks T.
implied_text: Same statistical electromagnetic population as the blackbody spectrum, now read as one integrated current. Small or few-mode objects fall off the T^4 envelope for the same reason a sparse cavity falls off the Planck curve.
description: The hardware is a black-enough, large-enough radiator. No universal area is extracted.
value_text: ε≈1 on Wien band; size ≳ λ_max(T); no universal area
notes: At 300 K, λ_max ∼ 10 μm. Finite-size and near-field corrections are real; they do not yield a single area number.

observed_text: The spectroscopic gap sets a frequency scale 2Δ/h of order 10^11 Hz for conventional metals (Δ in meV) and higher in cuprates. AC dissipation rises as the drive approaches that scale.
implied_text: DC zero resistance is the ω→0 output of a gapped condensate that still has an internal clock at 2Δ/h.
description: The condensate clock sits near 10^11 Hz in conventional metals; laboratory DC is already slow compared with that scale.
notes: Cuprate gaps sit higher. This is not a voltage-standard lock; that lives on josephson-effect.

observed_text: The coherence length spans three orders of magnitude across materials. Vortex pinning — the mesoscale reason R=0 can outlive complete expulsion — is not specified by Tc or Δ alone.
implied_text: QSA does not have a single buffer number for the condensate, and it does not yet have a buffer/barrier specification for the pinning step that protects R=0 after Meissner has failed.
description: The T/H/I collapses are located; hardware identity and mixed-state pinning are recorded as gaps rather than filled.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for these two gaps. This entry does not assert a pairing mechanism.

observed_text: Below Tc the DC electrical resistance falls below the instrument floor. A closed superconducting loop carries a persistent current for years with no measurable decay and no continuous voltage.
implied_text: Stable R=0 transport, and a persistent loop current at zero continuous voltage, inside the T / H / I envelope.
description: Superconductivity owns the R=0 artifact. Holding a persistent current costs zero continuous voltage.
notes: Split rule: meissner owns field expulsion / λ. Fluxoid integer is owned by flux-quantization.

observed_text: Tunneling and infrared absorption show a threshold 2Δ(T) that closes as T→Tc. The weak-coupling BCS ratio 2Δ(0)/kTc ≈ 3.52 is a fit to many conventional superconductors (Al close; Pb ~4.3).
implied_text: 2Δ is the energy threshold that suppresses ordinary quasiparticle transport. kTc, μ0 Hc (or Hc2), and the specimen Ic are the macroscopic envelopes that close that gap.
description: Zero resistance is protected by a measured gap that vanishes at Tc; the BCS ratio is a fit, not a universal node rule.
notes: Cuprates and other families that leave this ratio are not treated as contradictions. Pairing mechanisms are not QSA content.

observed_text: Type I: Al μ0 Hc ≈ 10.5 mT; Pb ≈ 80 mT; Sn ≈ 30 mT. Type II technical class: NbTi μ0 Hc2(4.2 K) ≈ 11 T; Nb3Sn μ0 Hc2(0) ≈ 25–30 T; YBCO μ0 Hc2,ab(0) of order 10^2 T.
implied_text: H > Hc (type I) or H > Hc2 (type II) destroys the condensate and restores finite R. Between Hc1 and Hc2, complete field expulsion has already failed while R=0 can still hold if vortices are pinned.
description: Field collapse of the condensate sits at Hc or Hc2; Meissner can fail earlier without ending R=0.
value_text: H > Hc (mT, type I) or Hc2 (tesla-scale, type II)
notes: value_si is NbTi μ0 Hc2(4.2 K). This entry owns R=0; meissner owns expulsion. Cross-cite type-ii-critical-field for the mixed-state window.

observed_text: Critical current Ic (or density Jc) is real and sharp on a given specimen, but it is not a material constant. It depends on cross-section, pinning landscape, field, and temperature. No single handbook Ic is quoted.
implied_text: I > Ic produces dissipation by pair-breaking, hot spots, or flux flow. That is a current-budget failure of the coherent channel.
description: Zero resistance ends when the transport current exceeds the specimen Ic. There is no universal current number.
notes: In type II the current cliff is often depinning rather than pair-breaking. Pinning itself is the consistency-gap row.

observed_text: Nb Tc = 9.25 K; Pb 7.2 K; Sn 3.72 K; Hg 4.15 K; Al 1.18 K; MgB2 39 K; YBCO ≈ 92 K; cuprates at ambient pressure extend to ~135 K (Hg-1223).
implied_text: T > Tc closes the gap and restores finite R.
description: Thermal collapse of zero-resistance transport at the material-specific critical temperature.
notes: These are material numbers, not a single universal Tc. value_si is Nb.

observed_text: Coherence-length class: Al ξ0 ~ 1.6 μm; Nb ξ0 ~ 40 nm; YBCO ξ_ab ~ 1.5–2 nm. Granular films and nanowires lose zero resistance when the coherent cross-section is under-provisioned.
implied_text: A coherent superconducting volume of order ξ in each direction is the buffer. That is a class, not a single measured cliff analogous to the 10–20 nm mirror.
description: Superconductivity needs a coherence-length buffer, but QSA does not have one hardware number for the condensate.
notes: value_si is Nb ξ0 ~ 40 nm, mid-class among the quoted materials. Closed-loop persistent current is owned by flux-quantization.

observed_text: There is no Josephson voltage-frequency lock (no e). Weak-link apertures in helium do produce an analogous current-phase oscillation; that is a related observation, not the primary artifact here. Second sound is a temperature wave in the two-fluid bookkeeping.
implied_text: Second sound is a hydrodynamic clock of the already formed superfluid, not the clock that opens the λ-point.
description: Superfluid 4He has no 2e/h lock; its internal hydro clock is not the Tλ specification.
value_text: no 2e/h lock; second sound is hydro
notes: Aperture analog belongs here as a related observation; the electrical specifications stay on josephson-effect.

observed_text: The load-bearing collapse is loss of ρs at Tλ (and of superflow at vc), not a measured charge gap of the superconducting kind. Why the λ-point sits at 2.17 K is not derived from node rules.
implied_text: The family name gapped is slightly loose here. The assignment follows the taxonomy rule — protected collective mode with a critical temperature — not a pairing-gap identification.
description: Chargeless superflow sits in gapped-coherence by collapse type, not by a pairing gap. The numerical origin of Tλ is also open.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Two-fluid bookkeeping is not used to derive Tλ. Dense interacting 4He is not the same hardware as a dilute alkali BEC.

observed_text: Circulation around a closed superfluid path is quantized: κ = h/m4 ≈ 9.97e-8 m²/s. Quantized vortices in the rotating liquid carry this increment.
implied_text: The chargeless counterpart of Φ0 is the circulation quantum h/m4 on a closed path.
description: Superfluid 4He emits an integer winding with measured quantum h/m4.
notes: Cross-check with flux-quantization is the existence of an integer winding, not identity of the two constants.

observed_text: Persistent currents circulate in a closed torus on laboratory timescales. Viscosity through a fine channel → 0 for the superfluid fraction below Tλ.
implied_text: Stable chargeless superflow and a persistent circulating integer at zero continuous power, inside T < Tλ and v < vc.
description: Holding superflow costs zero watts. The fountain and superleak responses are the same dissipationless output.
notes: Fountain head and vanishing viscosity are the same machine class. Contrast with BEC, which needs continuous cooling and trapping.

observed_text: Tλ = 2.17 K at saturated vapour pressure. The heat capacity has a λ-shaped singularity there. ρs → 0 as T → Tλ−, and ρs/ρ → 1 as T → 0.
implied_text: Tλ is the thermal cliff: ρs vanishes and the superleak / fountain / persistent-current responses go with it. Neither Tλ nor vc is a static anisotropy barrier; holding a persistent current still costs no continuous power while T < Tλ and v < vc.
description: The load-bearing thermal gate of chargeless superflow is the λ-point at 2.17 K.
notes: Under pressure the λ-line moves and ends when the liquid freezes. Two-fluid language is bookkeeping of ρs(T), not two substances.

observed_text: Above the λ-point the same liquid is an ordinary (if cryogenic) fluid: the superleak clogs, the fountain stops, and a finite viscosity returns.
implied_text: T > Tλ sets ρs = 0 and ends every superfluid response.
description: Thermal collapse of chargeless superflow at 2.17 K.
notes: Solidification across the melting curve is a coarser hardware removal.

observed_text: Superflow collapses above a critical velocity vc. Observed vc is geometry-dependent (channel size, film thickness, wall condition) and typically lies far below the Landau estimate taken from the roton minimum.
implied_text: vc is a velocity threshold that dumps superflow into a dissipative channel (vortex nucleation / coupling to the normal fraction), even though T < Tλ.
description: Superflow has a channel-dependent velocity cliff inside the T < Tλ envelope.
notes: Existence of a velocity cliff is high confidence; any one numerical vc is medium and is not quoted as a universal number.

observed_text: A connected volume of liquid 4He below Tλ, large enough to support a nonzero ρs. Superflow through packed powder and fine capillaries, and a climbing film, are the macroscopic demonstrations. There is no charge, no London λ, and no Meissner expulsion.
implied_text: The condensate buffer is a connected superfluid volume. The superleak or film is apparatus that the normal fraction cannot pass — a spatial filter, not the condensate buffer. Quantized circulation requires a closed path.
description: Chargeless superflow needs connected 4He with ρs > 0; it does not need an electromagnetic screening depth.
notes: Vortex cores are the chargeless analog of mixed-state defects. Do not collapse this hardware with dilute alkali BECs.

observed_text: The attempt time τ0 is a fitted constant, usually taken as 1e-9–1e-10 s; values down to 1e-13 s are used. Measurement windows run from 1e-12 s (neutrons) through 1e-9–1e-7 s (Mössbauer) to about 100 s (dc magnetometry).
implied_text: Two clocks, and the effect is their ratio: the attempt time and the observer's window. Blocking is a statement about the observer as much as about the grain.
description: The failure clock is the Néel attempt time compared with the measurement window, not the 28 GHz/T precession carrier.
value_text: τ0 ~ 1e-9–1e-12 s; windows 1e-12 s to years
notes: The same grain can be blocked in one apparatus and unblocked in another.

observed_text: The effective anisotropy of a 5 nm magnetite particle from a Néel–Brown fit is 356 kJ/m³ against the bulk 13.5 kJ/m³. Surface anisotropy, interactions and coupling to neighbours sit between unit-cell anisotropy and the observed blocking temperature.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer/barrier specification for that mesoscale Keff step.
description: The volume-and-time collapse does not depend on closing nanoparticle Keff; the mesoscale step remains underived.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Brownian relaxation in a fluid is a different machine and is not this entry.

observed_text: Holding the unblocked state costs no continuous power; the directional memory is simply gone. Zero continuous power on the blocked side as well.
implied_text: Neither the fluctuating unblocked ensemble nor the blocked parent latch draws hold power.
description: Holding either side of the blocking contour costs zero watts.

observed_text: On the unblocked side coercivity and remanence go to zero and M(H) is reversible, Langevin-like and scales with H/T. 4–5 nm magnetite: 294 Oe and 10.1 emu/g at 5 K against 12 Oe and zero at 300 K. Cooling or measuring faster restores the loop.
implied_text: Stable unblocked output is a zero-remanence ensemble curve plus the blocking surface, not a motor moment.
description: The unblocked grain emits a reversible Langevin curve and a blocking contour, not a usable remanent force.
notes: A single unblocked grain’s fluctuating moment is not a usable motor; the Langevin curve is already an ensemble average. Blocked side is the parent latch.

observed_text: Barrier ΔE = KV for uniaxial anisotropy and K1V/12 for cubic K1 < 0 (magnetite). Nd2Fe14B K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³; magnetite K1 = −1.35e4 J/m³. A 5 nm magnetite particle has an effective anisotropy of 356 kJ/m³, 26 times bulk. An antiferromagnetic matrix raises the blocking of 4 nm Co from 10 K to about 290 K.
implied_text: The barrier is a property of the grain and its surroundings together, not bulk K1 times volume.
description: The barrier that fails is KV, corrected for cubic symmetry, nanoparticle anisotropy and coupling to neighbours.
notes: The first version said the latch hardware is unchanged and only V differs. value_si is mid-range.

observed_text: τ = τ0 exp(KV/kT) against the measurement time: ln(τm/τ0) is 25.3 for 100 s, 40.3 for ten years and 2.3 for a Mössbauer window (τ0 = 1e-9 s). Recording media show decay onset at 35 ± 2 and need about 60 for ten-year storage. A 10 % change in diameter changes the retention time about four-thousand-fold.
implied_text: Thermal loss of direction on the observer's clock. Steep in size, with no critical value.
